title: The wrong number
setting: Evening at home. Kenji is slumped on the sofa with his phone when his mother sits down next to him, excited: she has made a friend at her piano lessons and got her number. She still calls every message on her phone a meeru.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji, chotto kiite. okaasan, piano naratteru desho? soko de tomodachi ga dekita no.
lines.ja: ケンジ、ちょっと聞いて。お母さん、ピアノ習ってるでしょ？そこで友達ができたの。
lines.kana: けんじ、ちょっときいて。おかあさん、ピアノならってるでしょ？そこでともだちができたの。
lines.english: Kenji, listen to this. You know I've been taking piano lessons? I made a friend there.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kyou ne, bangou oshiete tte ittara, sugu oshiete kureta no.
lines.ja: 今日ね、「番号教えて」って言ったら、すぐ教えてくれたの。
lines.kana: きょうね、「ばんごうおしえて」っていったら、すぐおしえてくれたの。
lines.english: Today I asked for her number, and she gave it to me straight away.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.kana: おかあさん、やるじゃん。

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: de, hiru ni sugu meeru okutta no. demo, mada kaeshite kurenai no.
lines.ja: で、昼にすぐメール送ったの。でも、まだ返してくれないの。
lines.kana: で、ひるにすぐメールおくったの。でも、まだかえしてくれないの。
lines.english: So I emailed her right away, at lunchtime. But she still hasn't replied.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: isogashii n desho. boku nanka, okaasan ni meeru kaesu no, mikka mo kakaru shi.
lines.ja: 忙しいんでしょ。僕なんか、お母さんにメール返すの、三日もかかるし。
lines.kana: いそがしいんでしょ。ぼくなんか、おかあさんにメールかえすの、みっかもかかるし。
lines.english: She's probably busy. I mean, it takes me three whole days to answer your emails.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji to issho ni shinaide. demo, nande meeru konai n darou.
lines.ja: ケンジと一緒にしないで。でも、なんでメール来ないんだろう。
lines.kana: けんじといっしょにしないで。でも、なんでメールこないんだろう。
lines.english: Don't lump her in with you. But why haven't I got an email back?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: a, sumaho natta yo. meeru kita n ja nai?
lines.ja: あ、スマホ鳴ったよ。メール来たんじゃない？
lines.kana: あ、スマホなったよ。メールきたんじゃない？
lines.english: Oh, your phone just went off. Isn't that an email?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: honto da, meeru kita! e, dare desu ka tte.
lines.ja: ほんとだ、メール来た！え、「誰ですか」って。
lines.kana: ほんとだ、メールきた！え、「だれですか」って。
lines.english: It is, an email! Wait, it says: 'Who is this?'

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: sore, chigau bangou ni meeru okutta n ja nai?
lines.ja: それ、違う番号にメール送ったんじゃない？
lines.kana: それ、ちがうばんごうにメールおくったんじゃない？
lines.english: Sounds like you sent your email to the wrong number.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: e, demo chanto bangou oshiete moratta yo. a, shichi to ichi, machigaeta kamo!
lines.ja: え、でもちゃんと番号教えてもらったよ。あ、「しち」と「いち」、間違えたかも！
lines.kana: え、でもちゃんとばんごうおしえてもらったよ。あ、「しち」と「いち」、まちがえたかも！
lines.english: What? But she gave me her number, properly. Oh! I might have mixed up 'shichi' and 'ichi'!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: aa, sore yoku aru. dakara nana tte iu n da yo.
lines.ja: ああ、それよくある。だから「なな」って言うんだよ。
lines.kana: ああ、それよくある。だから「なな」っていうんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah, that happens a lot. That's why people say 'nana' for seven.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: dou shiyou. shiranai hito ni meeru okutchatta. hazukashii!
lines.ja: どうしよう。知らない人にメール送っちゃった。恥ずかしい！
lines.kana: どうしよう。しらないひとにメールおくっちゃった。はずかしい！
lines.english: Oh no. I've sent an email to a total stranger. How embarrassing!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: raishuu mata au n desho? jaa, okaasan no bangou mo oshietara?
lines.ja: 来週また会うんでしょ？じゃあ、お母さんの番号も教えたら？
lines.kana: らいしゅうまたあうんでしょ？じゃあ、おかあさんのばんごうもおしえたら？
lines.english: You're seeing her again next week, right? Why not give her your number too, then?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: sou suru. a, sono mae ni, kono hito ni meeru kaesanakya.
lines.ja: そうする。あ、その前に、この人にメール返さなきゃ。
lines.kana: そうする。あ、そのまえに、このひとにメールかえさなきゃ。
lines.english: I will. Oh, but first I'd better reply to this person.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: うん。すぐ返してあげて。
lines.kana: うん。すぐかえしてあげて。
lines.english: Yeah. Write back to them right away.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji ni iwaretakunai. kesa okutta meeru mo, mada kaeshitenai desho.
lines.ja: ケンジに言われたくない。今朝送ったメールも、まだ返してないでしょ。
lines.kana: けんじにいわれたくない。けさおくったメールも、まだかえしてないでしょ。
lines.english: That's rich, coming from you. You still haven't answered the email I sent you this morning, have you?

questions.english: What happened to Mom's email to her new friend?
questions.ja: お母さんのメールは、どうなりましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんのメールは、どうなりましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan no meeru wa, dou narimashita ka?

choices.english: Her friend from piano finally wrote back, but had forgotten who she was.
She sent it to Kenji by mistake, which is why her friend never answered.
She got one digit of her friend's number wrong, so it went to a stranger.

questions.explanation: Lines 3-5: Mom got her new friend's number and emailed her at lunchtime, but no reply came (line 7). When an email finally comes, it says 'Who is this?' (line 9). Kenji guesses she sent it to the wrong number (line 10), and she realises she mixed up shichi (seven) and ichi (one) when her friend told her the number (line 11), so she has emailed a stranger (line 13). A is wrong because the 'Who is this?' comes from the stranger, not her friend. B mixes in a different email: the one Kenji hasn't answered is the one she sent him this morning (line 17).

questions.english: At the end of a party, Sora says: "Today was fun. Let's hang out again." Ask him for his number.
questions.ja: 今日、楽しかったね。また遊ぼうよ。
questions.kana: きょう、たのしかったね。またあそぼうよ。
questions.romaji: kyou, tanoshikatta ne. mata asobou yo.
questions.answer: Ask with oshieru ('tell'), not kudasai: bangou oshiete. Soften it with kureru: bangou oshiete kurenai?

modelAnswers.ja: うん！じゃあ、番号教えて。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah! Give me your number, then.

modelAnswers.ja: よかったら、番号教えてくれない？
modelAnswers.english: If you don't mind, could I get your number?

questions.explanation: Asking for someone's number is bangou oshiete, literally 'tell me your number', which is just what Mom said to her friend in line 3 (bangou oshiete tte ittara, sugu oshiete kureta). Giving your own uses the same verb: Kenji's okaasan no bangou mo oshietara? (line 14). English 'give' pulls toward kudasai, but bangou o kudasai sounds stiff, like a form being filled in.

questions.english: Why does Mom say she's embarrassed?
questions.ja: お母さんは、なんで「恥ずかしい」と言いましたか？
questions.kana: おかあさんは、なんで「はずかしい」といいましたか？
questions.romaji: okaasan wa, nande hazukashii to iimashita ka?

choices.english: She had sent a friendly email to someone she doesn't know.
A stranger had emailed her, and she couldn't remember who they were.
She had told Kenji all about her new friend before even getting a reply.

questions.explanation: Line 13: shiranai hito ni meeru okutchatta. meeru o okuru is her sending the email, with the person it went to marked by ni (shiranai hito ni, 'to someone I don't know'), and -chatta adds 'oops'. B turns the direction around: an email did come to her (meeru kita, line 9), but it was the stranger's answer to hers, and it was the stranger who didn't know her. C: she did tell Kenji about her friend, but that isn't what embarrasses her.

questions.english: When Mom's phone goes off, what does Kenji say?
questions.ja: スマホが鳴って、ケンジは何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: スマホがなって、けんじはなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sumaho ga natte, kenji wa nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: Didn't you just send an email?

questions.explanation: Line 8: a, sumaho natta yo. meeru kita n ja nai? In Japanese the email is the one that comes: meeru (ga) kita, 'an email came', and Mom answers honto da, meeru kita! A, okutta, is the other direction, her sending; Kenji does say it in line 10, but about her email going out to the wrong number, not about the phone going off. C, uketoru, is English 'receive' word for word, but it sounds stiff and is for parcels and documents, not emails.

questions.english: At work, Tanaka-san asks: "Did you see the email I sent yesterday?" You read it but forgot to answer. Apologise and say you'll reply right away.
questions.ja: 昨日送ったメール、見ましたか？
questions.kana: きのうおくったメール、みましたか？
questions.answer: Say you forgot to reply, using kaesu ('send back'): sumimasen, meeru o kaesu no o wasuretemashita. sugu kaeshimasu.

modelAnswers.romaji: sumimasen, meeru o kaesu no o wasuretemashita. sugu kaeshimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: すみません、メールを返すのを忘れてました。すぐ返します。
modelAnswers.english: I'm sorry, I forgot to reply. I'll get back to you right away.

modelAnswers.romaji: a, mimashita. sumimasen, ima sugu meeru kaeshimasu.
modelAnswers.ja: あ、見ました。すみません、今すぐメール返します。
modelAnswers.english: Oh, yes, I saw it. Sorry, I'll reply right now.

questions.explanation: Replying to an email is meeru o kaesu, 'send the email back': Kenji's okaasan ni meeru kaesu no, mikka mo kakaru (line 6) and Mom's kesa okutta meeru mo, mada kaeshitenai desho (line 17). Not meeru ni kotaeru: kotaeru is for answering questions (shitsumon ni kotaeru). And keep the s: kaeshimasu is 'I'll reply', but kaerimasu would be 'I'll go home'.
